title: DG embeddings preserving differential cokernels with two dual-free layers
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}A^j$ be an associative unital differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$: $d_A$ has degree $1$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^j a\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^j$. A right DG $A$-module $M$ is a graded right module with a degree-$1$ differential satisfying $d_M^2=0$ and $d_M(ma)=d_M(m)a+(-1)^j m\,d_A(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Use shifts $M[k]^n=M^{n+k}$ with differential $(-1)^k d_M$ and unchanged right action. Write $(A^\vee)^n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A^{-n},\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with $(d\lambda)(a)=(-1)^{n+1}\lambda(d_Aa)$ for $\lambda\in(A^\vee)^n$, and right action $(\lambda a)(b)=\lambda(ab)$. Products of graded modules are taken degree by degree. For every right DG $A$-module $M$ there are a DG map $u:M\to E$ and a short exact sequence of DG modules $0\to E^{\prime}\to E\to E^{\prime\prime}\to0$ such that $u$ is injective in each degree, the induced map $M^n/d_M(M^{n-1})\to E^n/d_E(E^{n-1})$ is injective for every integer $n$, and $E^{\prime},E^{\prime\prime}$ are each isomorphic as DG modules to a product of shifts of $A^\vee$. The displayed short exact sequence splits as a sequence of graded right $A$-modules, without requiring the splitting to commute with differentials. No boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub; the graded splitting follows from the graded injectivity of products of shifts of the character dual in section-modules-noncommutative-graded and Tag 09K2, lemma-source-graded-injective.

proof.text: Put $D=A^\vee$ and, for $k\in\mathbf Z$, $V_k=D[-k]$. For each $k$ define a right DG module $J_k$ by $J_k^p=V_k^p\oplus V_k^{p+1}$, componentwise action, and $d_J(v,w)=(d_Vv+w,-d_Vw)$. Squaring gives $(d_V^2v+d_Vw-d_Vw,d_V^2w)=0$. For homogeneous $a$ and $(v,w)\in J_k^p$, the Leibniz rules for $v\in V_k^p$ and $w\in V_k^{p+1}$ give $d_J((v,w)a)=d_J(v,w)a+(-1)^p(v,w)d_Aa$; the second component uses $-(-1)^{p+1}=(-1)^p$. Thus $0\to V_k\xrightarrow{v\mapsto(v,0)}J_k\xrightarrow{(v,w)\mapsto w}V_k[1]\to0$ is DG exact. The section $w\mapsto(0,w)$ is graded right $A$-linear. Its two layers are $D[-k]$ and $D[1-k]$. This realizes the two-layer disk construction in the first paragraph of the source proof with its graded splitting explicit.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub, first proof paragraph: the duals of Q_k and their two character-dual layers; explicit matrix form of the same disk.

proof.text: For every $\alpha=(k,\lambda)$ with $\lambda:M^k\to\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ additive, define a graded map $g_\alpha:M\to V_k$ by $g_\alpha^p(m)(a)=\lambda(ma)$ for $a\in A^{k-p}$. Associativity gives $g_\alpha(ma)(b)=\lambda(mab)=(g_\alpha(m)a)(b)$, so it is graded right $A$-linear. Put $t_\alpha=g_\alpha d_M-d_Vg_\alpha$, of degree $1$. Expanding the two Leibniz rules gives $t_\alpha(ma)=t_\alpha(m)a$: their $(-1)^p g_\alpha(m)d_Aa$ terms cancel. Therefore $f_\alpha(m)=(g_\alpha(m),t_\alpha(m))$ is a graded map $M\to J_k$. It is a DG map because $d_Jf_\alpha(m)=(g_\alpha d_Mm,-d_Vg_\alpha d_Mm)=f_\alpha d_M(m)$, using both squared differentials zero. In degree $k$, evaluation of its first component at $1\in A^0$ is $\lambda(m)$.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub, first proof paragraph: the map into the dual of the free sum of Q_k; coordinate expansion of each dual-disk map.

proof.text: Take the set $S=\coprod_{k\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M^k,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$ and put $E_0=\prod_{\alpha=(k,\lambda)\in S}J_k$, degree by degree, with componentwise differential and action. The maps $f_\alpha$ define a DG map $f_0:M\to E_0$. If $m\in M^p$ is nonzero, [lem-sfb-abelian-character-separates-points] applied to the additive group $M^p$ gives $\lambda(m)\ne0$. In the $(p,\lambda)$ coordinate the first component of $f_0(m)$ evaluates to $\lambda(m)$ at $1$, so $f_0(m)\ne0$. Additivity then proves degreewise injectivity. The coordinatewise sequence $0\to\prod_{S}V_k\to E_0\to\prod_{S}V_k[1]\to0$ is DG exact, with graded section $(w_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto((0,w_\alpha))_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub, first proof paragraph: injectivity into a product of dual disks and property (3); character separation is Tag 01DB, lemma-ev-injective, proof.

proof.text: Write $C_k=M^k/d_M(M^{k-1})$ and let $T$ be the set of all pairs $\beta=(k,\chi)$ with $\chi:C_k\to\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ additive. Let $q_k:M^k\to C_k$ be the quotient and put $\lambda=\chi q_k$. The formula of step 2 now gives a DG map $h_\beta=g_{(k,\lambda)}:M\to V_k$ without a disk. Indeed, for $m\in M^p$ and $a\in A^{k-p-1}$, $\lambda(d_M(ma))=0$ implies $\lambda((d_Mm)a)=(-1)^{p+1}\lambda(m d_Aa)$. On the other hand the shift and character-dual differential give $(d_Vg(m))(a)=(-1)^k(-1)^{p-k+1}\lambda(m d_Aa)=(-1)^{p+1}\lambda(m d_Aa)$. Thus $g(d_Mm)=d_Vg(m)$. Also $d_A1=0$, since the Leibniz rule at $1\cdot1$ says $d_A1=2d_A1$. Every boundary in $V_k^k=D^0$ evaluates to zero at $1$: for $v\in V_k^{k-1}=D^{-1}$, $(d_Vv)(1)=(-1)^k v(d_A1)=0$.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub, last proof paragraph, and Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free: the closed character gives a DG map to A^vee[-k]; its formula and boundary detection are verified here rather than used as an uncited lemma.

proof.text: Put $W=\prod_{\beta=(k,\chi)\in T}V_k$, $E=E_0\times W$, and $u=(f_0,(h_\beta)_\beta)$. These are DG modules and a DG map by the componentwise formulas. Let $E^{\prime}=(\prod_{\alpha=(k,\lambda)\in S}V_k)\times W$ and $E^{\prime\prime}=\prod_{\alpha=(k,\lambda)\in S}V_k[1]$. Include $E^{\prime}$ in $E$ using $(v_\alpha)\mapsto((v_\alpha,0))$ in its first factor and the identity on $W$; project $E$ to $E^{\prime\prime}$ by $((v_\alpha,w_\alpha),z)\mapsto(w_\alpha)$. The kernel is exactly $E^{\prime}$ and the graded right $A$-linear section is $(w_\alpha)\mapsto(((0,w_\alpha))_\alpha,0)$. This proves DG exactness and graded splitting without a theorem about exactness of arbitrary products. The first layer is a product of shifts of $D$ indexed by $S\amalg T$, and the second by $S$. Since $f_0$ is degreewise injective, so is $u$.

source.place: Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub, last sentence: add a product of character-dual shifts while retaining property (3); explicit kernel, graded section and product reindexing.

proof.text: The DG map $u$ induces maps $C_k\to E^k/d_E(E^{k-1})$. Suppose $\overline m\in C_k$ is nonzero. By [lem-sfb-abelian-character-separates-points] there is an additive $\chi:C_k\to\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$ with $\chi(\overline m)\ne0$. In the $\beta=(k,\chi)$ coordinate of $W$, the image of a representative $m$ is $h_\beta(m)$, whose evaluation at $1$ equals $\chi(\overline m)$. It cannot be a boundary in $V_k$, by step 4. If $u(m)$ were a boundary in $E$, its projection to this DG factor would be a boundary, a contradiction. Hence the induced map has zero kernel, and by additivity is injective for every $k$. Together with step 5 this is every required clause, with no boundedness or finiteness assumption.

Source check: Stacks dga.tex Tag 09KT lemma-good-sub, definition-shift, 09K2 and lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free, plus more-algebra.tex Tag 01DB lemma-ev-injective. The item statement is identical to live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit with no proof; it matches 09KT clauses (1)-(3), with 'admissible' written out as split in graded modules, and nothing is weakened. I rechecked every sign. In step 1 the disk J_k=V_k plus V_k^{+1} has square-zero differential, satisfies the Leibniz rule (second component -(-1)^{p+1}=(-1)^p), and the inclusion and the projection to V[1] (differential -d_V) commute with the differentials; the section is only claimed to be graded A-linear. In step 2, t=g d_M-d_V g is A-linear because the (-1)^p g(m)d_A a terms cancel, and d_J f=f d_M; evaluation at 1 recovers lambda. In step 4 the two signs agree: (-1)^k(-1)^{p-k+1}=(-1)^{p+1}. Also d_A1=0, so boundaries in D^0 vanish at 1, and no cocycle hypothesis is needed. Steps 3 and 6 use the new leaf only for its statement, applied to M^p and to C_k. Step 5 builds the kernel and the graded section coordinate by coordinate, with E' indexed by S plus T and E'' by S. The report's source error is correct: under M[k]^n=M^{n+k} the target must be A^vee[-k] (example A=Z, M=Z[-1]); the item, being an existence statement, is unaffected. The new node lem-sfb-abelian-character-separates-points is a statement-only, self-contained, exact Mathlib leaf: CharacterModule.exists_character_apply_ne_zero_of_ne_zero at lines 220-223, with CharacterModule defined at line 46 as maps to AddCircle 1, i.e. Q/Z. I tested it on Z/n, Z, Q and the zero group. The leaf is from Mathlib, so the route is unchanged; there are no tool_uses and no SGA citation. Minor: the report names citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are not in the commit.
